question: Which among the following elements possesses greater tendency to gain electrons?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Fluorine**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fluorine is the most electronegative element.**
 
• **As we move right in a period, the electronegativity keeps increasing up to the halogens**.
 
• This is because the number of electrons keeps increasing in the same valence shell so hold of the nucleus on the electrons is tight.
 
• **And as we move down in a group, the electronegativity decreases**. This is due to the fact that the number of shells keeps increasing down the group so the hold of the nucleus on the valence electron(s) keeps decreasing.
 
• Since **Flourine is the first member of the halogen family** (the rightmost group before noble gases), therefore it is the most electronegative element.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/de8e579bad676f371ea88208c06ec0e7035765745796574bdc93c1654f0bf5e9.png] [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nitrogen (N): **

 
 
• **Atomic Number:** 7
 
• **Properties:**
 
 
• Colorless, odorless, and tasteless.
 
• It makes up about **78%** of the Earth's atmosphere.
 
• It is inert and does not easily react with other elements due to its strong triple bond.
 
 
 
• **​**Has five valence electrons, usually sharing three to form stable bonds, leaving one lone pair. 
 
 
 
• **Carbon (C):**
 
 
• **Atomic Number:** 6
 
• **Properties:**
 
 
• Carbon exists in different forms such as graphite, diamond, and graphene.
 
• It has a high ability to form covalent bonds, allowing it to create a wide variety of organic compounds.
 
• The diamond form of carbon is the hardest natural substance.
 
 
 
• Has four valence electrons, allowing it to form four covalent bonds with other atoms. 
 
 
 
• **Oxygen (O)**:
 
 
• ​**Atomic Number:** 8
 
• **Properties:**
 
 
• Oxygen is colorless, odorless, and tasteless.
 
• It is highly reactive and forms oxides when it reacts with most elements.
 
• It is essential for combustion and respiration.
 
• Has six valence electrons, typically sharing two to form stable bonds.
